entry.title: POLYNICES: Transforming Hybrid Photonic Integration and Packaging

media:group.media:title: POLYNICES: Transforming Hybrid Photonic Integration and Packaging
media:group.media:description:
POLYNICES is developing innovative photonic packaging and integration technologies to simplify the assembly of next-generation hybrid photonic integrated circuits (PICs). By combining silicon nitride, indium phosphide, micro-optics, and terahertz components on a polymer-based electro-optic motherboard, the project aims to reduce photonic module costs while improving scalability, flexibility, and performance. POLYNICES is paving the way for advanced applications ranging from terahertz spectroscopy to quantum information processing, helping bring photonic innovations closer to large-scale industrial adoption.

entry.title: QSNP: Building the Future of Quantum-Secure Communications

media:group.media:title: QSNP: Building the Future of Quantum-Secure Communications
media:group.media:description:
QSNP is a European Quantum Flagship project bringing together 42 partners from 14 countries to develop the next generation of quantum-secure communication networks. By integrating advanced quantum technologies, including quantum key distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography (PQC), into existing telecom infrastructures, the project is helping protect critical data, networks, and services against future quantum threats. Fraunhofer HHI contributes its expertise in quantum communications and photonic technologies to support the development of secure, resilient, and sovereign European communication networks.

entry.title: SPRINTER: Photonics for Smart Industrial Networks

media:group.media:title: SPRINTER: Photonics for Smart Industrial Networks
media:group.media:description:
SPRINTER is a Horizon Europe project developing next-generation photonic technologies for smart manufacturing and Industry 4.0. By combining advanced photonic integrated circuits (PICs), optical transceivers, and optical switching solutions, the project aims to deliver high-capacity, low-latency, and energy-efficient industrial communication networks. Fraunhofer HHI will contribute to the project with its expertise in high-speed photonic components and hybrid integration technologies. Supporting applications such as automation, IoT, AI, and digital twins, SPRINTER is paving the way for reliable, time-deterministic connectivity and the digital transformation of Europe's industrial infrastructure.

media:group.media:title: Next-Generation Ultra-High-Speed Microwave Photonic Integrated Circuits
media:group.media:description:
PATTERN is advancing ultra-high-speed microwave photonic integrated circuits (PICs) through hybrid integration of thin-film lithium niobate, indium phosphide, and high-performance electronics. By developing new PIC building blocks, design kits, and packaging solutions for frequencies beyond 100 GHz, the project is paving the way for future applications in 6G, quantum technologies, LiDAR, sensing, and optical communications. Fraunhofer HHI contributes its expertise in integrated photonics, hybrid PIC technologies, and photonic integration.

media:group.media:title: Networked Robotics Testbed
media:group.media:description:
Controlling multiple autonomous robots to solve tasks collaboratively is challenging due to unreliable and resource-limited wireless communication, as well as the inherently distributed nature of information. Our Networked Robotics Testbed enables researchers to experiment with algorithms that jointly consider control, communication, and computation in multi-agent systems, incorporating both real-world and virtual agents to support scalable experimentation. Built around the modular balancing robot Bilbo, the platform captures practical trade-offs between fast local control (self-balancing) and slower distributed information fusion over the air. Using this platform, we showcase our fast and scalable consensus protocol (paper and video) that leverages Over-the-Air Computation (OTA-C) technology for efficient information fusion in a multi-robot target-tracking application. The testbed enables rapid prototyping and evaluation of next-generation algorithms for collaborative robotic systems operating over wireless networks.

entry.title: Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation: A Visual Introduction | XAI Methods Explained

media:group.media:title: Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation: A Visual Introduction | XAI Methods Explained
media:group.media:description:
Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) is a foundational method in Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Originally introduced in 2015 by researchers at Fraunhofer HHI in collaboration with TU Berlin, LRP explains neural network predictions by propagating relevance scores backward through the model’s layers. This video provides a clear visual introduction to the core principles of LRP, illustrating how relevance is redistributed across layers to highlight the input features most responsible for a given prediction. It is the first episode in our series on XAI methods and neural network interpretability, with upcoming videos covering related techniques such as Concept Relevance Propagation (CRP).

entry.title: Final 6G-RIC Advisory Board Meeting & Workshop: Technology Advancements for 6G & Beyond

media:group.media:title: Final 6G-RIC Advisory Board Meeting & Workshop: Technology Advancements for 6G & Beyond
media:group.media:description:
After 4.5 years of pioneering research, the 6G Research and Innovation Cluster (6G RIC) will complete its initial phase at the end of 2025. During this time, we have advanced key technologies that will shape the next generation of mobile networks. For Germany and Europe, developing new technologies is vital to secure prosperity, innovation leadership, and technological sovereignty. That is why 6G RIC is more than a research project — it is a strategic investment in the future.
Our achievements were showcased at the final 6G RIC Advisory Board Meeting and Workshop, held on October 14–15 at the Science Tech Space at @ Fraunhofer HHI in Berlin under the theme: “Technology Advancements for 6G and Beyond.”
More than 130 leading experts from the global 5G and 6G community joined us to exchange ideas and set strategic directions for the future of mobile communications.
The event featured: - Inspiring keynotes and thought provoking plenary discussions - Parallel sessions on technological, societal, and industrial perspectives - Over 27 live demonstrations of cutting edge prototypes and applications Highlights included breakthroughs in: - Microelectronics and PHY Layer Technologies (e.g., Sub-THz communication) - Network as a Sensor and Digital Twins (integrating communication and sensing) - AI for Communications and Edge Intelligence
We also explored future priorities such as knowledge transfer, ecosystem sustainability, and the role of 6G in healthcare (e.g., telemedicine) and other emerging fields.
Looking ahead, 6G-RIC has paved the way for #xG RIC, a permanent center of excellence that will continue research beyond 6G, driving innovation and strengthening digital sovereignty for the long term.
A big thank you to the Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) and all our partners for their outstanding collaboration!

entry.title: Discover Hidden Concepts in Large AI Models With SemanticLens | AI Interactive Demo

media:group.media:title: Discover Hidden Concepts in Large AI Models With SemanticLens | AI Interactive Demo
media:group.media:description:
SemanticLens is a universal explanation method designed to systematically understand and validate the internal components of modern AI models, such as neurons, attention heads, and convolutional filters.
As AI models grow more powerful and are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, understanding what each component is doing is essential for safety, transparency, and compliance (e.g., under the EU AI Act).
🔍 What is SemanticLens?
SemanticLens maps the hidden knowledge encoded in neural networks into a structured, human-interpretable semantic space, enabling new and powerful operations:
🔎 Search: Query the model like a search engine “Does the network know that a bluish veil is linked to melanoma?” 🧾 Describe: Auto-label and explain the functional role of components 📊 Compare: Analyze representations across models and layers 🔒 Audit: Validate alignment with expectations and safety requirements 🧠 Evaluate Interpretability: Measure clarity and polysemanticity of components
Try the interactive demo: https://semanticlens.hhi-research-insights.de Read the paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05398

entry.title: AI-based QoS Prediction for Real-time Sidelink Offloading

media:group.media:title: AI-based QoS Prediction for Real-time Sidelink Offloading
media:group.media:description:
This video showcases our work on Quality of Service (QoS) prediction for real-time sidelink offloading in 5G private networks, where Artificial Intelligence (AI) enables proactive switching between traditional uplink/downlink and sidelink (direct device-to-device) communication to ensure seamless connectivity, lower latency, and improved energy efficiency.
The demo features a mobile robot performing remote inspection, utilizing AI-driven QoS prediction to maintain optimal communication. The prepared demo setup is based on NVIDIA ARC-OTA for the 5G base station and an in-house sidelink implementation compliant with the 3GPP Release 16 standard.

media:group.media:description:
The video presents an O-RAN demo based on the open-source research platform developed at Fraunhofer HHI. It demonstrates an F1 handover in O-RAN, with the user resources transferred from one DU-RU path to another. This process can be triggered, for example, by a near-real time control loop running in an xApp.
Find more information here: https://6g-ric.de/

Das Video präsentiert eine O-RAN-Demo, die auf der Open-Source-Forschungsplattform des Fraunhofer HHI basiert. Es zeigt einen F1-Handover in O-RAN, bei dem die Nutzerressourcen von einem DU-RU-Pfad auf einen anderen übertragen werden. Dieser Prozess kann beispielsweise durch eine nahezu echtzeitfähige Kontrollschleife in einer xApp ausgelöst werden.
Besuchen Sie unsere Website, um weitere Informationen zu erhalten: https://6g-ric.de/
